newsitem.title: USA: Seven ex-SEC chiefs oppose Calif. proposition 211.
newsitem.headline: Seven ex-SEC chiefs oppose Calif. proposition 211.

text.p: Seven former chairmen of the Securities and Exchange Commission have joined the agency's current chairman, Arthur Levitt, in opposing California's Proposition 211.
The seven former chiefs of the securities watchdog were led by David Ruder, now a law professor at Northwestern University, who contacted the six others to get their views.

Ruder said in a letter Thursday to Levitt that he got in touch which the former SEC heads after Levitt expressed opposition to the initiative and joined President Bill Clinton in urging California voters to oppose it.
The other former SEC chairmen who joined Ruder were James Sinclair Armstrong, Richard Breeden, Hamer Budge, G. Bradford Cook, Roderick Hills and Harold Williams.
Levitt made his stand public after Rep. Anna Eshoo, a California Democrat, asked him for his views on the proposal in a letter on October 15.

In opposing Proposition 211, Levitt said it may skew the balance in competing concerns -- protecting companies from frivolous lawsuits while allowing private actions for meritorious cases brought by investors --addressed by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act passed last year.

"If adopted, the propositon would actually encourage litigation by adding a new private right of action to California's securities laws which is broader than in any other state," Levitt said in a letter to Eshoo.
Levitt said California state courts could become a magnet for class action suits, giving the local rule a nationwide impact.
